featured_reviews.review_text:
We took our new Labrador puppy to this clinic and we were guided really well for everything and all our questions and queries were answered satisfactorily. Very cooperative staff and doctors.

Edit: The doctor gave vaccines to the new puppy despite of informing about the bleeding in stool, later after checking with blood tests it was found that the dog had parvo virus infection and that they won’t provide further treatment. The puppy passed away within 7 days of bringing him home. We later admitted him to Parel Animal Hospital. Now when I am aware of parvo infection I strongly recommend to not give 9/11 when the dog shows symptoms, it worsens the infection.

Had the assistance been better the puppy would not have died. It was our first puppy and for our next dogs we never visited this clinic ever again.

featured_reviews.name: Natasha Pink
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. Akshay 😇 I can’t find words to describe this man! Such words have not yet been invented in any language! My story is 7 months long.
On April 6, one of my children all got sick at once, 6 puppies near my house. I urgently flew from Mumbai home to Varanasi, what I saw tore my heart into small pieces! They were paralyzed! I realized that this was a nervous plague. But I have never encountered this before, I don’t know how to treat it, and the most annoying thing is that we don’t have doctors in Varanasi who would be so professional. It was hell. Between changing diapers and calming the children, in tears, I read veterinary forums and literature. I called hundreds of veterinarians in Russia. And most of them recommended euthanization. I just can’t explain to the Russian people that according to our religion, we cannot take anyone’s life. I tried... I tried everything! Everything I could! We even got the serum delivered from Mumbai. I went to a human medical school, but out of desperation, I learned how to give IVs to dogs. Nobody wants to help me, everyone shrugged their shoulders, but I was simply dying from pain and hopelessness. I prayed day and night for Shiva and Ganesha to decide and either take them away or for them to go to recovery. Day after day, week after week, month after month. I did massages and continued to fight the plague. The children died in my arms, and by lowering them into the Ganges, I also lowered part of my heart. Of all the people, only Snezhana was able to defeat the plague! But she also remained bedridden. Bedsores, heart and kidney failure, then diarrhea and constipation began. The only thing that remained unchanged was his excellent appetite.How many tears I shed is known only to the gods. And the day came when my visa expired.... I took Snezhana to animal Rescue....
And I thought that I would never see her again. In Rescue, no one had time for massages and her bedsores became bone-chip. I was dying sitting in Russia, on my knees at the consulate so that they would quickly check my documents. But they kept dragging on (they were embarrassed by my appearance, although I offered to put me on a polygraph and they were convinced that I had never used anything), at that moment they found a tumor on my dad, and it just pulled me to the window, just to jump and not suffer anymore. But I continued to pray and Ganesha brought me a Russian guy who agreed to watch Snezhana and do a massage. I rented them a room in the house where Snezhana was born (my room is also there). But he didn’t have enough energy for a massage. Her paws became like those of a female praying mantis. I watched the video every day and lost hope.... Until Ganesh Chaturthi came! A Pandit from India came to Moscow, I went to pray, we got into a conversation and he asked, “During the yagya, was it uncomfortable for you to sit?”, I told him my story of a spinal fracture and how I stood up thanks to Ganesha and also mentioned that acupuncture helped me a lot!
The text continues in the photo, the whole story didn't fit.

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. We informed this situation of Leopard at every visit to Dr. Sunetra, but she recommended to force feed our Leopard. Later on our Leopard left with no energy to walk on his own and lift his neck, he even started heavy breathing. After informing this situation to Dr. Sunetra, she then advised us to put saline for his recovery but nowhere had she conveyed that Leopard’s health is deteriorating & he needs hospitalization. At this time, she was going out of town & was not available for 4-5 days.
Since, Dr. Sunetra was not available, we went to other Vet doctor who knew Leopard's medical history. This doctor told us to continue saline treatment twice a day for at least 4-5 days. Here the blood test was also done to examine the condition of our Leopard, where the report came with alarming & critical output depicting WBC increased & Platelets dropped to severe condition. Even this doctor also not recommended that our Leopard require hospitalization. This was the 11th day after operation.
The 12th day story (i.e. 1st July 23) of our Leopard was worst. The morning session of his saline was completed & even this second doctor went out of town for 3-4 days without recommending hospitalization. By evening, somewhere from 4:30pm, the heavy breathing became worse & we could not see his pain. We started calling Dr. Sunetra, but her phone was not reachable, so we text her on WhatsApp along with Leopard’s blood report. Since no response from doctor, with Leopard, we rushed to a Vet hospital, where he was admitted with a note by the doctors, like heavy breathing & drop in body temperature, which was very critical condition. He was kept in ICU incubator with oxygen supply to ease his breathe & improve his body temperature. The hospital doctors even told us that there are chances that the infection might have spread into blood. Unfortunately battling with pain & breathing problem our Leopard passed away on the same day around 11 pm.
There are certain questions for Dr. Sunetra;
# Why you haven't included any medicine for infection post-surgery?
# Why you did not advised us prior to start saline, when we informed you that Leopard lost his appetite?
# Why you did not look closely if the infection was spreading in the body? If you think it wasn't then why did he lost his appetite, had weakness, got fever, started heavy breathing?
# Why you took everything so lightly and casually in his case? Was it because it was a stray cat?

The doctor’s entire focus was on the operated area and the wound & the rest health parameters were ignored completely.

Better critical-care protocols

Proper IV handling skills

Clear communication with pet parents

More compassion and less commercial attitude

At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

Veterinary medicine, especially in very young kittens with severe systemic illness, can sometimes involve sudden deterioration despite timely medical care and supportive treatment.

We completely understand the grief and distress associated with losing a young pet. However, we strongly deny allegations of negligence or intentional carelessness by our doctors or staff. featured_reviews.name: Sabah Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Update on 16/03/26: Wildvets has now demanded Rs. 1 Lakh in defamation & Rs. 25k for their legal fees in sending me a civil court summon for an honest & truthful review of their practice.

Requesting all pet parents to be extremely cautious while approaching such an establishment.

I have an ongoing treatment for 2 of my cats- there is no doubt that there is  quite of a lot of immoral practice.

21/06/25 - Took my cat “Honey” with a complain of blood in his urine. Drs prescribed a stool, urine, radiograph, & blood test; we agreed & did the radiograph & blood test right there.

Radiograph received on 21st itself, with missing diagnosis that their drs insist we can’t read

Blood reports were a nightmare to get - first admin staff keeps insisting that they’ve sent it over email. I’m receiving other emails from them, they also have the correct email so I guessed it’s some tech issue & requested if she can whatsapp instead. The sheer arrogance of this woman. Downright refusing to do so; Wildvets never gives a hard copy of their reports, & this person is refusing to share it over whatsapp, how am I supposed to see the results? After much arguing she finally agreed to share over whatsapp - what she shares is a stool report from 2024; keep in mind I sent a blood sample in 2025. Explaining her this was another mountain to climb.

23rd - I took my cats Honey and Cream for a sono as Cream also started to show some issues. They did their sono at the clinic itself, in the morning. As of now - 24th June evening - I’m yet to see these reports, keep in mind most places (human or animal) produce these in less than an hour. On 23rd I was told these reports will come by the evening, now I’m being told it will take 3 DAYS?

To top this, their drs injected both my cats with meds their team REFUSED to write down. After we asked the receptionist why so, she exclaimed that all this is in their system. Basically to trap you from going to other vets. Till date I have not recvd a written prescription of what was administered to them. Imagine going to a hospital & them injecting you with whatever, then refusing to disclose? Where is the transparency? Does this not smell of malpractice?

Their drs, despite so many days have been unable to give a clear explanation. Upon seeing the cat’s sono at the clinic they claimed “one was worse than the other”, I’m sorry these educated professionals are calling “worse than the other” a diagnosis? Till date not one of them has explained what results came out of the urinary or stool test. Or print on a paper? What does wild vets charge a premium for if a report cannot be printed & given? How poor is this place?god only knows how long will the sono take.

I am speaking with 2 other external vets, both of them appalled at Wild Vet’s behavior. Keep in mind I’m not even paying these drs & they have managed to chart a treatment plan, something wild vets is still unable to do. All we do here is x no. of tests to crank up the bill, with drs giving 0 explanations, admin staff disrespecting you at every chance they get, & a potential malpractice of injecting animals with substances that can make their situation worse. They won’t let you take a simple file to store prescription without paying for it, but they will ensure to milk you dry out of money until your wallet dies or your pet.

I’m sure Wildvets will have a long defensive answer to give, I’m keen on knowing what justifies rudeness, lack of communication, & refusal to write down administered meds

featured_reviews.name: Preeti Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took my dog, Coco, to Wild Vets for a rabies titre test as part of the requirements for traveling to Dubai. Unfortunately, I had a disappointing experience with their service and communication.
Firstly, I was not informed that the sample could be sent to a lab in Bangalore, which is recognized by the UAE government. Instead, they chose to send it to a lab in London that charges £70 (as per the lab's website). However, I was charged ₹24,800 by Wild Vets, which is a significant markup with no clear explanation provided.
The sample was taken on August 9th, and I was told that I would receive the results within 3 to 4 weeks. As the three-week mark passed, I began following up and learned from the London lab that the results had already been sent to Wild Vets. Despite this, I did not receive the results promptly.
When I contacted Dr. Amrita for clarity, I was shocked by how rudely I was spoken to, especially considering the amount I had paid for the service. Due to these delays and lack of proper communication, I was forced to postpone my travel plans. I finally received the test results after five weeks — far beyond the promised timeline.
This entire experience has left me disappointed and frustrated. I no longer feel confident in the professionalism or reliability of the doctors at Wild Vets.
